meaning:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;]
weakness, frailty, sickness: Luk.13:11-12, Jhn.11:4, Act.28:9, Rom.6:19 8:26, 2Co.11:30 13:4, Gal.4:13 (MM, see word), Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.5:5, 1Co.2:3 15:43, 2Co.12:9; pl., Mat.8:17, Luk.5:15 8:2, 2Co.12:5 12:9-10, 1Ti.5:23, Heb.4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)

elsewhere.note: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”
But the report concerning him spread much more, and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.
I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh, for as you presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness…
I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.
but you know that because of weakness in the flesh I preached the Good News to you the first time.
